Study visit on mangrove carbon credits in Trat postponed, and points prepared for the PM2.5 report to the Senate
se: The meeting considered 2 matters. First, preparations for a study visit on a mangrove carbon credit project in Trat. The meeting agreed to postpone the trip from 11–13 December 2026 to 29–31 December. The visit will look at how people and local communities take part in conserving, restoring and managing mangroves and the coast in a sustainable way while earning income from carbon credits, in communities in Khao Saming and Laem Ngop districts, and at a community enterprise on Ko Chang that makes products from coconut shells, which creates jobs and cuts pollution from burning. Second, preparing questions and answers for presenting the study report on fine particulate matter of 2.5 microns or less (PM2.5) in the critical areas of Bangkok, its surrounding provinces and the upper North to the Senate. Subcommittee members concerned were given responsibility for each point.
it: Study visit on a mangrove carbon credit project, Trat: postponed from 11–13 December 2026 to 29–31 December

Preparing to present the PM2.5 dust study report, and approving a study visit on mangrove carbon credits
se: The meeting considered 2 matters. First, preparation for presenting the study report on fine dust of up to 2.5 microns (PM2.5) in the critical areas of Bangkok, its vicinity and the upper North. The meeting discussed 10 questions that may be raised when the report is presented, such as why the problem returns every year, what the report adds to the government's existing national agenda action plan, which measure is most urgent, cost-effective alternatives to burning for farmers such as biochar, which central data (Big Data) should be kept, and the conditions for using sections 44 and 45 of the Enhancement and Conservation of National Environmental Quality Act B.E. 1992 in critical areas. Second, a study visit on mangrove forest carbon credit work: the meeting approved a visit to Trat from 11 to 13 December 2026, and set the next meeting for Thursday 19 November 2026.

Preparing to present the PM2.5 report, and adding proposals to reduce burning on farmland
se: The meeting prepared to present the study report on PM2.5 dust in the critical areas of Bangkok, its vicinity and the upper North, and agreed to set questions so that the Senate debate leads to policy proposals that can be put into practice. It also considered views received when the report was presented to the committee on 20 October 2026, such as reducing burning on farmland through awareness, communication and incentives, which the subcommittee will add to the report to make it clearer. The next meeting was set for Thursday 29 October 2026.

Draft report on PM2.5 dust, and preparing to present it to the Senate
se: The meeting considered the draft study report on fine dust of up to 2.5 microns (PM2.5) in the critical areas of Bangkok, its vicinity and the upper North, and gave views on presenting it to the Senate. Besides the presentation slides, it suggested preparing about 4–5 key questions and answers that are short and help senators and the public understand the report's main points, especially details that cannot all be covered in the limited presentation time. The next meeting was set for Thursday 22 October 2026.
it: Draft study report on PM2.5 dust in the critical areas of Bangkok, its vicinity and the upper North: presenting it to the Senate and preparing questions and answers
